title: Scan line video synth
technique: A 1970s-style analogue video synthesizer: a hidden source picture is redrawn as glowing scan lines in 3D, each line pushed up and back by the brightness beneath it.
music: Bass bends the whole picture sideways, kick hits make the lines stand taller and flash, and snare hits tear bands of lines sideways. Hi-hats break the lines into gaps, the live spectrum ripples along them, and each new section of the song turns the picture to a new angle and rolls it once.
as_processor: Redraws the picture it is given as glowing scan lines in 3D: brighter parts of the picture lift the lines higher, and in some takes the lines take on the picture's colours.

takes.name: Portrait
takes.description: A 3D model drawn as a green wire relief on a tilted plane, seen from a three-quarter view; the classic look of the technique.
words: A hidden picture of a 3D model is redrawn as 110 scan lines.
The brighter the picture under a line, the higher it lifts.

takes.name: Colouriser
takes.description: Hundreds of fine lines seen face-on and close up, almost a solid picture, with brightness split into hard bands of flat colour and the picture slipping vertically on the bar line.
words: 230 scan lines seen face on. Brightness is cut into 5 bands,
each given one flat colour. Bass bends the picture sideways.

takes.name: Mandala
takes.description: Two dozen lines made from plain oscillators are fed back on themselves like a camera pointed at its own monitor, building a mirrored pattern with three to eight-fold symmetry.
words: 24 lines of sine waves and words, fed back like a camera aimed
at its own monitor. Each pass turns them 1/N of a circle.

takes.name: Landscape
takes.description: No model: printed phrases fill the frame as raised amber wire lettering on a plane laid back like terrain.
words: 90 scan lines cross a page of words that is never shown.
Bright parts push the lines up off it. Kicks push further.

takes.name: Waterfall
takes.description: No picture at all: the last few seconds of the music's spectrum are drawn as a white mountain range, with nearer ridges hiding the ones behind.
words: Each of 72 lines is the sound spectrum a moment ago: newest
in front, low notes in the middle. Near ridges hide far ones.

takes.name: Negative
takes.description: The polarity is reversed, giving dark wires of a model on a lit beige field with a phrase printed flat in red behind them, set off-centre.
words: Polarity reversed: 110 scan lines of a 3D model, dark on a
lit field. A keyer prints these words flat in red behind.

takes.name: Macro
takes.description: A few dozen fat red lines running vertically in extreme close-up, with nearer lines hiding those behind, so the subject reads as abstract.
words: 46 fat scan lines run top to bottom over a 3D model, very
close. A black surface under the lines hides the ones behind.

takes.name: Monitor wall
takes.description: The same signal shown on a bank of four, nine or sixteen small screens, each set up differently in colour, brightness, zoom and stability.
words: One scan-line signal on 4, 9 or 16 tubes, no two set up alike:
colour, brightness, hold, mirror, zoom and polarity differ.

takes.name: Rings
takes.description: The scan lines are bent into concentric circles, each ring its own hue, giving a rainbow relief of the model on black.
words: The scan is re-patched from rows to 72 rings over a 3D model.
Each ring has its own hue. Brightness lifts it towards you.

takes.name: Drum
takes.description: Phrases are raised around a slowly turning cylinder of cyan rings with pink lettering, tilted and off-centre.
words: 130 rings stacked into a cylinder, a page of words wrapped round.
Bright parts push the rings out. A black drum hides the back.
